title: 4DN Falcon Analysis
bodyHtml:
4DN Falcon Analysis

What is the likelihood that a gene is connected to a trait, and which specific variants drive that connection?

Here we analyze 4D Nucleome (4DN) data using FALCON, a powerful Bayesian method that transforms complex genetic data into actionable insights. By integrating GWAS/EWAS summary statistics, linkage disequilibrium, variant annotations, and variant-to-gene (V2G) maps, it calculates a confident genetic support score for genes of interest. FALCON distinguishes real signals from noise and integrates annotation-driven learning when available. FALCON’s hybrid variant-to-gene approach combines evidence-based scoring with robust distance modeling, delivering precise gene-trait associations. Results include posterior probabilities of gene involvement, fine-mapped effect sizes, and finely resolved variant-to-gene links, providing a statistically rigorous view of how genes and variants contribute to human phenotypes and traits.

For this specific analysis, FALCON model's variant-to-gene (V2G) linkage was informed exclusively by evidence-based scores derived from enriched chromatin interaction links from human experiments hosted on the 4DN Data Portal. This approach leverages data on the three-dimensional organization of the genome to connect variants to the distant genes they may regulate.
